measured_path.description: Where the checkout happened to live on the measuring host. Informational only: a committed manifest must validate in any checkout, so nothing resolves against this.

version.description: Release version of the measured revision, when the measured project has one. An unpublished library records null here; a versioned one records both this and the commit.

upstream.description: The optional second recorded library revision: a baseline the measured library is compared against, when the campaign's descriptor declares `identities: [library, upstream]`. A campaign may record one revision or two; the toolkit requires neither count, so this property is allowed rather than required. When present it is validated and resolved exactly like `library`.

ref.description: The ref the revision was pinned by, typically a release tag, so the pin is reproducible and not only a hash.

measured_path.description: Where the checkout happened to live on the measuring host. Informational only, like `library.measured_path`.

vendor.description: The BLAS/LAPACK library the measured provider was linked against, as the harness reported it from the vendor's own introspection. A measurement whose vendor cannot be named is not evidence, so `validate_run.py` refuses a manifest whose declared engines include a vendor arm and whose `vendor` is absent. A run whose suite declares no vendor engine omits the property entirely rather than recording a null one; absence, not an empty identity.

config.description: The build configuration string the vendor reports, for example `OpenBLAS 0.3.32 NO_AFFINITY COOPERLAKE MAX_THREADS=24`.

corename.description: The kernel the vendor's runtime dispatched to. Not necessarily the target the build was configured for: an AVX-512 host can select an Intel-named kernel, which is a fact to record rather than an error to hide.

build_env.description: The build-time environment the campaign declares for the vendor library, for example `OPENBLAS_DYNAMIC_ARCH=1`. It is recorded because it decides what was linked: without it a from-source OpenBLAS guesses a target from the build host, which is not a build a measurement should depend on.

local_commits_allowed.description: Present (true) only when the run was recorded with `--allow-local-commits`: a source commit it records may exist only in a local checkout, so CI cannot resolve it. Such a run is a throwaway probe and `publish_report` refuses to publish it.

outputs_dirty.description: The recorder's own output locations (`excluded_outputs`) held uncommitted changes. They are not harness source, so `dirty` ignores them.

excluded_outputs.description: Campaign-relative paths left out of the `dirty` check: the results root, the result pages directory and the index, as the descriptor declares them.

excluded_sibling_outputs.description: Campaign-relative output paths declared by the other campaign descriptors of the same harness repository, also left out of the `dirty` check. `outputs_dirty` does not cover them.

power.description: Power/frequency controls in force while measuring, read from sysfs when the host exposes them.

role.description: development or measurement: a development host's pages are provisional and are superseded by the measurement host's dataset.

l3_domains.description: Per-domain L3 description from the hardware profile. On a host whose cores share one L3 this repeats `l3`; on a heterogeneous host (different L3 sizes per core group) it is the fact that decides whether a thread set spans one domain or two.

observer.description: The observing side's CPUs as recorded, not assumed: `affinity` is the recording process's own sched_getaffinity, `free_cpus` the CPUs outside every measured L3 domain. Absent from manifests recorded before this field existed; the refusal that admitted those runs still applied.

note.description: How the budget was enforced, when that needs saying: for a vendor-backed provider the harness sets the vendor's own thread count and reads it back, so the row's label is a fact rather than a hope.

tag.description: The release tag an external baseline was built from, when it was built from one. A commit and a tag together say which release the bytes came from; either alone says less.

sha256.description: Hash of the artifact linked for an external provider. It says which bytes were measured, which neither a commit nor a tag does for a built native library.

sibling_aware.description: Whether the idle gate also checked the SMT siblings of the measured CPUs. A busy sibling contends with the physical core being measured, and upstream's script checked only the listed logical CPUs, so this is stated rather than assumed.

run_spec.description: What this particular run covered. A subset of the suite declaration is a valid run: the campaign is not run in full on every profile.

populations.description: The resolved populations this run covered: one `family x shape grid x regime` block per declared population, after group expansion. Coverage is a statement about these, not about a scalar size knob.

n.description: Matrix dimensions: `N` for square, `MxN` for rectangular, `MxKxN` for a three-index operation such as a multiply-accumulate, which cannot be written as two.

skipped.description: `family/shape` pairs the harness reported as not applicable to that family. Recorded, not inferred: a family the provider rejects is coverage the run did not have.

order.description: The extra declared axis this run covered, when the harness measures one (the memory order, `c`/`f`). It is part of a cell's identity, so it is recorded, and the declaration is read back rather than the harness command.

suite_sha256.description: Hash of the suite declaration in force when the run was taken. Evidence is immutable and declarations are not: without this, a manifest and a later declaration can disagree with no way to tell which moved.

verification.description: The grid the verify checked, when it is narrower than the timing grid.
